citation: Miller, S., Biggart, A., Sloan, S., & O'Hare, L. (2017). Success for All: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Independent evaluators: Centre for Evidence and Social Innovation, Queen's University Belfast.) ERIC ED581417; trial registration ISRCTN97011396.
report_number: EEF project: Success for All (SfA); ERIC ED581417; ISRCTN97011396
design: School-level two-armed cluster RCT (effectiveness trial), business-as-usual control; 54 primary schools (27 vs 27), ~1767 Reception pupils; whole-school literacy programme (Success for All) with embedded teacher training (16 days + ongoing in-school support over 2 years) delivered via the Success for All Foundation; Reception-to-Year-1 (K-2); England. Same study as registry row 109 (sloan_2018).
problems:
DUPLICATE of row 109 (sloan_2018) -- EEF Success for All; do not double-count. Identity decision and supporting evidence below. NO effect sizes extracted here on purpose, to avoid double-counting the Success for All effects already extracted in data/extracted/pilot/sloan_2018.json (row 109).

DECISION: registry row 79 ('Miller et al. 2017') is the SAME primary study as registry row 109 ('Sloan et al. 2018'): the EEF Success for All evaluation, authored Miller, Biggart, Sloan & O'Hare (2017). The full PDF (data/fulltext/sloan_2018.pdf) title page reads 'Success for All -- Evaluation report and executive summary, July 2017; Independent evaluators: Dr Sarah Miller, Dr Andy Biggart, Dr Seaneen Sloan, Dr Liam O'Hare (Queen's University Belfast)'. Lead author = Sarah Miller, year = 2017, so the short-cite 'Miller et al. 2017' (row 79) and the short-cite 'Sloan et al. 2018' (row 109) both resolve to this one report. The meta-analysis authors appear to have entered the same study twice under two different cites (a duplicate in their included-study list), with inconsistent moderator codings (see below).

EVIDENCE -- codings compared (registry studies.csv / supplement S3.1+S3.2):
  Identical method/setting fields (S3.1) for BOTH rows: assignment_unit=School; research_design=RCT; publication_status=Unpublished; grade_level=K-2; ses=Average/High SES; targeted_population=All; tpd_trainer=Res/Dev.
  Treatment fields (S3.2) DIFFER between the two rows:
    row 79 (Miller 2017): tpd_goal=Comprehensive approaches; tpd_duration=Long; n_principles=Four; coaching=1, performance_standards=1, self_regulation=1, cooperation=1.
    row 109 (Sloan 2018): tpd_goal=Other; tpd_duration=Short; n_principles=Zero; coaching=0, performance_standards=0, self_regulation=0, cooperation=0.
  Which coding actually matches Success for All? Row 79's. The Visscher et al. (2025) main text (p.3) names Success for All as its canonical example of 'TPD for comprehensive approaches', stating it 'includes cooperative learning, student performance monitoring, student tutoring and cooperation with parents and the school community' (citing Borman et al., 2007). That maps to goal=Comprehensive approaches, cooperation=1, performance_standards=1 -> the FOUR-principle coding of row 79, NOT the zero-principle coding of row 109. The SfA report itself (sloan_2018.pdf pp.6-9) describes a whole-school reform with cooperative learning at its core, continuous assessment/performance monitoring, an in-school SfA coordinator/coaching, and 16 days of training plus ongoing support over two years (= Long, not Short). The sibling Slavin cooperative-learning whole-school study in the same dataset, Stevens & Slavin 1995 (row 116), is coded identically to row 79 (Comprehensive / Four principles), confirming this is how the team coded an SfA-type comprehensive cooperative-learning reform. Row 109's Other/Short/Zero coding is the anomalous/duplicate entry.
  No separate, distinct 'Sloan et al. 2018' K-2 whole-school literacy RCT exists: targeted web searches (EEF, ERIC, Google Scholar) for a Sloan-2018 trial all resolve back to Success for All (the only other distinct Sloan-coauthored 2018 trial is the Roots of Empathy SEL study, grades 3-4, social-emotional -- not K-2 literacy, does not match row 109). The Queen's Belfast team's other distinct EEF literacy report, Reciprocal Reading, is already separately captured as row 85 (ohare_2019). This rules out row 109 being a third, different Queen's Belfast study and supports row 79 == row 109 == Success for All.

CONSEQUENCE for the merge: count the Success for All effect sizes ONCE (from row 109 / sloan_2018.json). This miller_2017.json (row 79) carries zero effect sizes. NB: if the central analysis instead prefers to attach SfA to the row with the correct moderator codings, row 79 holds the better codings (Comprehensive/Long/Four) while row 109 (sloan_2018.json) holds the extracted numbers -- either way the study is a single SfA report and must not be double-counted.
